newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BCE wheat, maize futures see limit falls.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BCE wheat, maize futures see limit falls.

text.p: Maize futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) joined wheat's lower trend on Thursday, dealers said.
"The...decline in maize futures has finally begun," said Antal Szoke of Agrimpex.
Maize prices for March, May and July maturities dropped some 400 forints -- the most permitted in one day on the BCE -- while November maize eased 250 forints. March ended at 20,100 forints.
Traders do not foresee buyers for one million tonnes of surplus Hungarian maize as good harvests elsewhere have saturated potential markets.
Szoke added maize prices were not likely to find support above some 17,000 forints in the next few months.
Feed wheat prices also fell by the 400-forint limit for all maturities traded on Wednesday. Feed wheat closed at 26,600 forints for January, 20,500 for July and at 22,400 for December, 1997.
Milling wheat eased 300 to 400 forints, with the January maturity closing at 27,540 forints, July at 21,600 and December 1997 at 24,200 forints.

Dealers expect milling wheat prices to continue to fall but noted that future demand was hard to predict as, for example, smaller mills have not yet appeared on the market. --Sandor Peto, Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040
